scope: Final visible Draft, exact source/article/action/deployed bytes, core #578/#590/#599-#601 lifecycle and implementation records, the complete open daily-logger review-data PR set and intended Draft lifecycle, workstation-yuri #12 lifecycle, current review schema/discovery and held-candidate custody. Read-only review; no article revision or acceptance, finding disposition, action admission or settlement, readiness, merge, workflow dispatch, runtime, or scheduling authority.

findings.title: The #599 replay reported no blocking findings
findings.location: Line 38 says both #599 and #601 review rounds found concrete blocking defects.
findings.explanation: PR #599 reports that its independent Yojimbo replay passed the two cases with no blocking findings. The four blocking defects belong to PR #601, not #599.
findings.correction: Say both PRs record independent replay or review activity, but only #601 records four blockers; describe #599 as a clean bounded replay.

findings.title: The HTTP restriction governs an outbound endpoint, not a worker listener
findings.location: Lines 24 and 44 say unrestricted HTTP exposed the worker's HTTP surface to subnet callers.
findings.explanation: The final #601 settings parser validates the endpoint used by the worker client and permits HTTP only for loopback hosts; remote endpoints require HTTPS. The PR does not add a worker-owned HTTP listener.
findings.correction: Describe the defect as permitting an insecure remote HTTP endpoint for worker traffic; do not claim an exposed inbound worker surface or a direct Unix-socket replacement.

findings.title: PR #600 predates #601's merge and already records a completed replay
findings.location: Lines 64, 82 and 85 say #600 opened 13 minutes after #601 merged, lacks independent review, and should receive /review next.
findings.explanation: PR #600 opened at 2026-11-13T22:36:52Z; #601 merged at 2026-11-14T00:24:06Z, about 1 hour 47 minutes later. #600's public body already records independent Yojimbo execution, both cases passing, and no blocking findings.
findings.correction: State that #600 was staged before #601 merged and already records an independent replay; remove /review core#600 unless a new owner requests a different gate.

findings.title: PR #590 states its owner-review hold
findings.location: Line 66 says core #590 has no stated hold reason.
findings.explanation: PR #590 is a Proposed, unnumbered ADR whose unchecked test-plan item is owner review; acceptance then numbers it with /adr accept and applies the glossary terms.
findings.correction: Report #590 as waiting on the explicit owner-review and ADR-acceptance gate, not as an unexplained open draft.

findings.title: The review-data set and intended Draft lifecycle are misreported
findings.location: Lines 68, 82 and 91 say eight audit drafts span #529-#543 and treat the lack of a merge criterion or owner as an unexplained queue.
findings.explanation: Eleven review-only Draft PRs were open: #515, #524, #526, #529, #530, #533, #535, #537, #539, #541 and #543. #529 is November 5 and #530 November 4. Their PR bodies intentionally reserve revision, acceptance and merge authority and name supervised finding disposition as the next step.
findings.correction: Report eleven open review-data Draft PRs with the correct date mapping and explain that Draft/open is the publication state pending supervised disposition, not evidence of a missing merge owner.

findings.title: workstation-yuri PR #12 had already merged
findings.location: Lines 70 and 89 say #12 is pending owner review and merge and blocked only on owner action.
findings.explanation: PR #12 merged at 2026-11-12T02:13:02Z, more than two days before the article capture. Its pre-merge body wording is historical after that lifecycle event.
findings.correction: Report #12 as merged and remove it from open work and retained continuation context.

findings.title: The public record does not independently authenticate the named review sessions
findings.location: Lines 17, 24, 38 and 56 present the Yojimbo replays and #601 re-verification as independent review facts.
findings.explanation: The shared-account PR bodies report separate Claude/Codex sessions and opaque HelpDesk message numbers, but #599, #600 and #601 have no GitHub review submissions and the HelpDesk reports are not publicly linked. The implemented safeguards are visible; distinct provider, session and machine identity are not independently authenticated by the public record.
findings.correction: Attribute replay and re-verification to the PR author record or link a public source-bound report; do not treat a shared account or model agreement as independently authenticated identity.
